newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Three foreign insurers to enter Brazil's market.
newsitem.headline: Three foreign insurers to enter Brazil's market.

text.p: Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV, American International Group Inc affiliate American Life Insurance Co and Metropolitan Life Insurance Co have requested authorization to operate in Brazil's life insurance market, said Brazil's insurance watchdog Susep.

A Susep official, who asked not to be named, said the three foreign insurers have sent their request earlier this week. Susep is expected go over their paperwork and rule on their requests within two or three months, she added. She noted that the watchdog has never refused a request before.
"Usually these firms's requests are adequate to the Brazilian law and there will be no problem in giving them permission to operate in Brazil," she said.

The firms are eyeing Brazil's promising insurance market, which is expected to grow at impressive rates of 15 percent annualy over the next few years due to increasing demand for life, pension and health plans.

ING has requested authorization to operate in Brazil's life insurance market, she said, while American Life through its unit AIG Life Companhia de Seguros and Metropolitan Life have sent requests to operate in the Brazilian life insurance and private pension plan markets, she added.
Brazil's insurance premiums reached 13.6 billion reais ($13 billion) in the first 11 months of 1996, according to Susep.
